findings.body: The join returns no rows, so indexing `[0]` and then `['id']` raises on nil before the uncategorized fallback can run; the deployment migration aborts.
findings.failure_mode: Database migration fails with a nil dereference on ordinary installations that have never configured an embed category.
findings.impact: The join returns no rows, so indexing `[0]` and then `['id']` raises on nil before the uncategorized fallback can run; the deployment migration aborts.
findings.root_cause: The migration dereferences the first row of an optional category lookup without checking whether a row exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the query result in a variable and safely handle an empty result before deriving the ID, then use the existing uncategorized fallback when no matching category is found.
findings.title: Handle an unset legacy embed category during migration
findings.trigger: Run the migration on an installation where `embed_category` is blank, points to a deleted/renamed category, or otherwise has no matching category row.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 11 verbatim shows `WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` - the code dereferences [0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows. The fallback at line 14 only runs if category_id == 0, not if the query failed.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing embedding integrations stop being authorized immediately after the settings-to-table migration.
raw_findings.impact: The raw URL is persisted instead of the normalized hostname, while `record_for_host` later queries by `URI(...).host`; no row matches and that previously allowed host is denied after the upgrade.
raw_findings.root_cause: The migration bypasses the model's normalization callback and inserts legacy setting strings verbatim.

raw_findings.body: Imports for that host use whichever duplicate row the database returns first, so the displayed mapping is not reliably the category used for newly created embedded topics.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Per-host category routing becomes ambiguous and can route posts to an unintended category.
raw_findings.impact: Imports for that host use whichever duplicate row the database returns first, so the displayed mapping is not reliably the category used for newly created embedded topics.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new host table permits duplicate host values while lookup deliberately selects only a single unspecified first record.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce a case-insensitive unique host mapping with a model validation and a database unique index, and normalize host casing consistently.
raw_findings.title: Do not allow duplicate host mappings with conflicting categories
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator creates two allowed-host records for the same hostname and assigns them different categories.

raw_findings.body: `URI#host` drops the port, so the lookup compares `example.com` with the stored `example.com:8443` and rejects an entry that passed the model's port-supporting validation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid configured non-default-port embedding hosts cannot embed comments.
raw_findings.impact: `URI#host` drops the port, so the lookup compares `example.com` with the stored `example.com:8443` and rejects an entry that passed the model's port-supporting validation.
raw_findings.root_cause: Authorization lookup discards the port even though stored host values and validation permit ports.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalize and compare host plus explicit port (with appropriate default-port normalization), or disallow ports in validation if port-specific entries are not supported.
raw_findings.title: Preserve the configured port when looking up an allowed host
raw_findings.trigger: Configure an allowed host with a port, such as `example.com:8443`, then request embedded comments from `https://example.com:8443/article`.

raw_findings.body: The validation callback calls `sub!` on nil and returns a 500 response instead of a normal validation error for the missing host.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Malformed but routine API input causes an unhandled server exception.
raw_findings.impact: The validation callback calls `sub!` on nil and returns a 500 response instead of a normal validation error for the missing host.
raw_findings.root_cause: The normalization callback assumes `host` is always a String before validations have established that invariant.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the normalization callback for nil/blank values and let the format/presence validation report an invalid host.
raw_findings.title: Avoid a nil dereference when the host attribute is omitted
raw_findings.trigger: POST or PUT an embeddable-host payload that includes the object but omits its `host` field.

raw_findings.title: Return not-found rather than crashing on updates to deleted hosts

raw_findings.title: Return not-found rather than crashing when deleting an unknown host

raw_findings.title: Keep truncation expansion disabled when no hosts remain

The model's before_validation strips scheme/path, but migration bypasses model. If legacy setting contains 'http://eviltrout.com', it's stored verbatim while record_for_host uses URI.host for lookup, causing mismatch. Realistic trigger for existing installations.

validated_findings.body: Imports for that host use whichever duplicate row the database returns first, so the displayed mapping is not reliably the category used for newly created embedded topics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Per-host category routing becomes ambiguous and can route posts to an unintended category.
validated_findings.impact: Imports for that host use whichever duplicate row the database returns first, so the displayed mapping is not reliably the category used for newly created embedded topics.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new host table permits duplicate host values while lookup deliberately selects only a single unspecified first record.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce a case-insensitive unique host mapping with a model validation and a database unique index, and normalize host casing consistently.
validated_findings.title: Do not allow duplicate host mappings with conflicting categories
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator creates two allowed-host records for the same hostname and assigns them different categories.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about duplicate host mappings is speculative. The patch doesn't show any unique constraint being removed or evidence that duplicates are a realistic concern. The absence of a unique index is a design choice, not necessarily a defect introduced by this patch. No evidence duplicates would actually occur in practice.

validated_findings.body: `URI#host` drops the port, so the lookup compares `example.com` with the stored `example.com:8443` and rejects an entry that passed the model's port-supporting validation.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Valid configured non-default-port embedding hosts cannot embed comments.
validated_findings.impact: `URI#host` drops the port, so the lookup compares `example.com` with the stored `example.com:8443` and rejects an entry that passed the model's port-supporting validation.
validated_findings.root_cause: Authorization lookup discards the port even though stored host values and validation permit ports.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalize and compare host plus explicit port (with appropriate default-port normalization), or disallow ports in validation if port-specific entries are not supported.
validated_findings.title: Preserve the configured port when looking up an allowed host
validated_findings.trigger: Configure an allowed host with a port, such as `example.com:8443`, then request embedded comments from `https://example.com:8443/article`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 14 shows `host = uri.host` which extracts only hostname without port. Line 2 shows validation regex allows ports `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`. If admin configures 'example.com:8443', it passes validation and is stored, but record_for_host compares URI.host (no port) against stored value (with port), causing lookup failure.

validated_findings.body: The validation callback calls `sub!` on nil and returns a 500 response instead of a normal validation error for the missing host.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Malformed but routine API input causes an unhandled server exception.
validated_findings.impact: The validation callback calls `sub!` on nil and returns a 500 response instead of a normal validation error for the missing host.
validated_findings.root_cause: The normalization callback assumes `host` is always a String before validations have established that invariant.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the normalization callback for nil/blank values and let the format/presence validation report an invalid host.
validated_findings.title: Avoid a nil dereference when the host attribute is omitted
validated_findings.trigger: POST or PUT an embeddable-host payload that includes the object but omits its `host` field.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 6 shows `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` in before_validation callback. If host attribute is nil (omitted from request), sub! on nil raises NoMethodError. The validates_format_of runs after before_validation, so nil isn't caught first. Realistic trigger via malformed API request.

validated_findings.body: `save_host` receives nil and dereferences it, producing a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale admin edit requests fail as internal server errors.
validated_findings.impact: `save_host` receives nil and dereferences it, producing a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The update action accepts a nil result from `where(...).first` without handling it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `find`/`find_by!` or explicitly render a not-found response before calling `save_host`.
validated_findings.title: Return not-found rather than crashing on updates to deleted hosts
validated_findings.trigger: An admin submits an update after another admin has deleted the selected host, or sends a PUT for an unknown ID.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 10 shows `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `save_host(host)` at line 11. If no record exists, host is nil, and save_host will call methods on nil causing 500 error instead of proper 404 response.

validated_findings.body: The following `host.destroy` call is invoked on nil and yields a 500 response instead of a not-found response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale admin delete requests fail as internal server errors.
validated_findings.impact: The following `host.destroy` call is invoked on nil and yields a 500 response instead of a not-found response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The destroy action does not handle the absence of the requested record.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `find`/`find_by!` or explicitly render a not-found response before calling `destroy`.
validated_findings.title: Return not-found rather than crashing when deleting an unknown host
validated_findings.trigger: An admin deletes a host that was already removed in another session, or issues DELETE for a nonexistent ID.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 15 shows same pattern: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `host.destroy` at line 16. If record doesn't exist, host is nil and destroy on nil causes 500 error. Same root cause as candidate 5 but different action (destroy vs update) at independently fixable site.

validated_findings.body: The existing embedded topic is still marked expandable even though embedding has been disabled by removing every allowed host; previously the empty host configuration made this predicate false.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The UI exposes expansion behavior after administrators have disabled embedding by deleting all allowed hosts.
validated_findings.impact: The existing embedded topic is still marked expandable even though embedding has been disabled by removing every allowed host; previously the empty host configuration made this predicate false.
validated_findings.root_cause: The replacement predicate removed the only check that embedding is configured and did not add an equivalent table-backed check.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Require an enabled embeddable-host configuration (for example `EmbeddableHost.exists?`) in addition to `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`.
validated_findings.title: Keep truncation expansion disabled when no hosts remain
validated_findings.trigger: Enable `embed_truncate`, create an embedded topic, and then delete the last EmbeddableHost record.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that removing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check causes incorrect behavior is questionable. The old check was for a site setting that's being migrated to a table. The new behavior (checking embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?) is intentional - if a topic was embedded, it should remain expandable. Deleting hosts doesn't un-embed existing topics.

validated_findings.body: `categoryId` remains null on the component, so this overwrites the saved host's category with undefined and the newly added row displays no category until a reload despite being stored as Uncategorized.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The admin UI immediately shows an incorrect category relationship for valid newly saved hosts.
validated_findings.impact: `categoryId` remains null on the component, so this overwrites the saved host's category with undefined and the newly added row displays no category until a reload despite being stored as Uncategorized.
validated_findings.root_cause: The client uses the request-side category value instead of the server-side value, even though the controller substitutes a default for blank values.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: After the save resolves, derive the category from the returned/updated `host.category_id` rather than from the pre-save component value.
validated_findings.title: Use the server-assigned default category after saving a blank selection
validated_findings.trigger: Add a host without selecting a category, causing the server to assign `uncategorized_category_id` for the blank `category_id`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim assumes categoryId is null when saving without selection, but line 26 shows `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))` in edit action. For new hosts, the controller at line 25 sets default category_id. The client-side display issue is minor UI inconsistency, not a data corruption bug, and the server returns correct data.
